data.title: Nevus comedonicus — viva
data.summary: Nevi & hamartomas · 15 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Nevus comedonicus** (Nevi & hamartomas)_

**Q1. What is nevus comedonicus?**
- Rare organoid epidermal (follicular) naevus with clusters of dilated follicular openings plugged with dark keratin (comedo-like), arranged in a linear/Blaschkoid band, usually unilateral on face, neck, trunk or upper limbs; present at birth or childhood; NEK9 mosaic mutation

**Q2. Clinical variants.**
- Non-inflammatory (comedones only)
- Inflammatory: cysts, pustules, abscesses, scarring (acne-like) — often from puberty
- Nevus comedonicus syndrome: with CNS (seizures), skeletal (scoliosis, polydactyly), ocular (cataract) anomalies — epidermal naevus syndrome

**Q3. Histopathology.**
- Wide, deep invaginations of epidermis filled with laminated keratin; rudimentary hair shafts or sebaceous lobules; follicular rupture with inflammation in inflammatory type

**Q4. Differential diagnosis.**
- Acne vulgaris/comedonal (not linear), chloracne, Favre–Racouchot syndrome (solar comedones in elderly), familial dyskeratotic comedones, Dowling–Degos (comedo-like papules), linear porokeratosis, porokeratotic eccrine naevus (palms/soles), verrucous epidermal naevus

**Q5. Management.**
- Comedo extraction, topical retinoids, keratolytics (salicylic, lactic acid), ammonium lactate
- Inflammatory: oral antibiotics, isotretinoin
- Definitive: surgical excision; dermabrasion, CO2/Er:YAG laser, electrocautery

**Q6. What is the genetic basis?**
- Post-zygotic mosaic mutation of NEK9 (also FGFR2 in some) in the follicular unit — a follicular hamartoma; NEK9 mutations also seen in nevus comedonicus syndrome

**Q7. What is nevus comedonicus syndrome?**
- Nevus comedonicus with extracutaneous anomalies — CNS (seizures, developmental delay, EEG abnormalities), ocular (cataract), skeletal (scoliosis, hemivertebrae, syndactyly) — an epidermal naevus syndrome; needs neurological/orthopaedic assessment

**Q8. Complications.**
- Inflammatory variant with recurrent cysts, abscesses, sinuses and scarring (acne conglobata/hidradenitis-like), secondary infection; rarely malignancy in long-standing lesions

**Q9. Dermoscopy findings.**
- Multiple keratin plugs ('comedo-like openings') — dark-brown to black round plugs, clustered in a linear distribution

**Q10. Describe the clinical features.**
- Grouped dilated follicular openings filled with dark keratin plugs (comedo-like), linear/ unilateral along Blaschko lines on face, neck, trunk, upper arms; present at birth or childhood (50% by age 10)

**Q11. Treatment options in detail.**
- Topical retinoids (tretinoin, tazarotene), keratolytics (salicylic acid, ammonium lactate), comedone extraction, oral isotretinoin for inflammatory variant, Er:YAG/ CO2 laser, dermabrasion, surgical excision of small lesions

**Q12. Histopathology in detail.**
- Wide, deep invaginations of epidermis filled with laminated keratin plugs (dilated follicular ostia) with absent or rudimentary hair shafts; small sebaceous glands may open into base; secondary inflammation and cysts

**Q13. Differential diagnosis in detail.**
- Acne vulgaris/ comedonal acne (bilateral, symmetrical, adolescents), chloracne (halogenated hydrocarbons), familial dyskeratotic comedones, Favre–Racouchot (solar comedones around eyes in elderly), linear porokeratosis, epidermal naevus, Dowling–Degos (comedo-like papules)

**Q14. What is Favre–Racouchot syndrome?**
- Nodular elastosis with cysts and comedones on periorbital/ malar skin of elderly sun-exposed smokers; treat with retinoids, comedone extraction, sun protection, smoking cessation

**Q15. Define and classify genodermatoses (PYQ).**
- Inherited disorders with skin manifestations — by inheritance: AD (NF1, TSC, Darier, Hailey–Hailey, EBS), AR (XP, lamellar ichthyosis, PXE, oculocutaneous albinism), X-linked recessive (X-linked ichthyosis, Fabry, Wiskott–Aldrich), X-linked dominant (IP, Goltz, CHILD, Conradi), mitochondrial, mosaic (epidermal naevi, McCune–Albright, Proteus)
- By function: keratinisation (ichthyoses, PPK), adhesion (EB), pigmentation (albinism, piebaldism), DNA repair (XP, Bloom), connective tissue (EDS, PXE, cutis laxa), tumour syndromes (NF, TSC, Gorlin), vascular (HHT), ectodermal dysplasias, immunodeficiency

## Quick spotter facts
- Linear cluster of comedones on a child's neck — nevus comedonicus

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Epidermal naevi — organoid). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
